title: His greatest contribution: high notes
summary: He was said to be first to play above C, and recalls Armstrong's advice.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: What do you see as being your greatest contribution to America's music? How would you see that? I mean, that's, we all agree that you made one. That's evident everywhere. I mean, everyone just recognizes that you did, and they have different things to say. Okay. I like the music to dance to. I like this. I like "Tippin'In". I like "Tuxedo Junction". You know, whatever. But, just from your standpoint. Looking back on all of it, I mean, what would you see is that unique, kind of stamp or contribution that you made?

I don't know. We were talking about high notes, or doing anything about that. But, during my time of the year when I came up playing C's above C's, well, you didn't have the trumpet players doing it then. They said that I was the first one to start to do that.

Well, they were saying, what gave me the Gabriel part, that's (inaudible). So, they said that I started that and, you know, did it. Although, I think that's one of them that I can remember. It's like Louis came over to me and said now you made your point. Now, kind of take it easy, save it. Save your chops for many years. So, don't burn yourself out.
